summary: A letter-style note from people at Atomic Energy Commission sites, including Argonne, Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory and New York University, who were planning to join the ARPANET. They needed remote job entry (RJE) early, and propose a lightweight way to do it over FTP, using reserved pathname conventions such as RJE.JOB, RJE.PR and RJE.STAT, instead of implementing a separate RJE protocol.

eli5.summary: Some research labs were about to plug into the network and wrote to say what they most needed: a way to send jobs to big computers from far away. They suggest using the file-sending tool with special file names, like a mailbox for jobs.

subtitle: Proposal to implement remote job execution over FTP using special filenames.

tldr.problem: New Atomic Energy Commission research labs (Argonne, Lawrence Berkeley Lab, and NYU) were joining the ARPANET but needed remote job entry (RJE) capability immediately, and did not want to implement a separate RJE protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The proposal uses FTP (File Transfer Protocol) with special site-dependent pathname conventions: RJE.JOB for submitting jobs, RJE.PR/RJE.PU/RJE.MT for retrieving output, and RJE.STAT for checking job status. Job execution parameters are specified in standard control cards transmitted with the file.
tldr.outcome: Sites could implement remote job submission with minimal additional protocol work by reusing FTP, allowing new ARPANET participants to get research computing capability quickly.

facts.label: New sites
facts.value: Argonne, Lawrence Berkeley Lab, New York University

today: RFC 551 represents an early example of protocol pragmatism: using an existing standard (FTP) in creative ways rather than building a brand new protocol. This approach would become common in ARPANET and Internet design, where new services were often layered over existing infrastructure.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: Several Atomic Energy Commission installations were planning to join the ARPANET, including Argonne National Laboratory (IBM 360/195), Lawrence Berkeley Labs (CDC 7600), and New York University (CDC 6600). These sites had diverse research applications that made early implementation of remote job entry (RJE) capability essential. While they accepted the necessity of implementing FTP (File Transfer Protocol) to participate on the network, they wanted to avoid having to implement a separate RJE protocol in addition to FTP. This RFC proposes a solution that leverages FTP to accomplish RJE by using special filename conventions.
sections.eli5: Three new computer sites wanted to join the network. They needed to be able to send jobs to their big computers from a distance, but they did not want to write a whole new program just for that.

sections.title: The Proposed Solution
sections.content: The proposal uses FTP with special local pathname conventions to implement RJE. To submit a job for execution, a user sends a STOR (store) command to a file named RJE.JOB followed by the rest of the pathname, with the job queued for execution. To retrieve a remote job's output, a user can retrieve files using STOR or RETR commands with special names: RJE.PR for print output, RJE.PU for punch output, and RJE.MT for magtape output. A user can check the status of a submitted job by sending a RETR command for RJE.STAT, which causes the server to create a status file and transfer it to the user. Job execution parameters are not part of the protocol itself, but instead are specified in standard site-dependent control cards that are transmitted with the job file. These control cards also determine where the output should go. The user's FTP login credentials are used only to validate the data transfer, not to determine whether the job has permission to execute.
sections.eli5: When you send a file to a computer named RJE.JOB, it runs the file as a job. RJE.STAT gets you information about your job. This reuses the file-transfer system, so you do not need a new protocol.

sections.title: Advantages of This Approach
sections.content: This proposal allows research sites to implement remote job execution without developing a separate RJE protocol. By building on FTP, which sites must implement anyway, the protocol overhead is minimized. The use of reserved pathname conventions (RJE.JOB, RJE.PR, RJE.PU, RJE.MT, RJE.STAT) provides a clear semantic separation without requiring protocol changes. Site-dependent control cards and job parameters are handled through standard conventions, allowing flexibility in how individual sites configure job execution, priority, output handling, and resource allocation.
sections.eli5: This way, sites do not have to build something brand new. They just add special filenames to their existing file-sending system, and it works for running jobs.
